### HDB Financial Services Q2 profit jumps 34% to ₹780 crore 

Non-banking financial company HDB Financial Services on Wednesday reported a 34.2 per cent surge in profit after tax to Rs 780 crore in the September quarter of FY27 driven by higher loan demand and lower provisions.

The financial services entity had earned a PAT of Rs 581 crore in the year-ago period.

Its net interest income rose 15.6 per cent to Rs 2,534 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, up from Rs 2,192 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, the firm said in a stock exchange filing.

HDB Financial Services’ total income rose 12 per cent to Rs 3,188 crore for the quarter under review from Rs 2,851 crore in the year-ago period. (PTI) 
- October 14, 2026 17:35

### BHEL shares surge nearly 5 pc on robust Q2 numbers 

Shares of state-owned BHEL on Wednesday surged nearly 5 per cent after the state-owned firm reported a two-fold jump in consolidated net profit for the September quarter.

The stock jumped 4.86 per cent to Rs 463.50 on the BSE. During the day, it climbed 4.88 per cent to Rs 463.60 -- the 52-week high level.

At the NSE, the stock rallied 4.89 per cent to end at Rs 464.

The company’s market valuation surged by Rs 7,486.44 crore to Rs 1,61,393.64 crore.

BHEL on Wednesday reported a two-fold jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 820.94 crore for the September quarter, driven by higher income from key business verticals such as power and industry. (PTI)

### Tata Technologies Q2 profit rises 4% to ₹171 crore, revenue up 28% yoy 

Tata Technologies Limited reported a consolidated net profit of ₹171.44 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from ₹165.50 crore in the same quarter last year, a rise of about 4 per cent. Revenue from operations grew sharply to ₹1,698.80 crore from ₹1,323.33 crore a year ago, an increase of nearly 28 per cent. 

The Board of Directors approved the unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results at its meeting on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, which ran from 9:30 a.m. to 3:46 p.m. The results were reviewed by the Audit Committee a day earlier and carry an unmodified conclusion from statutory auditors BSR & Co. LLP. 

For the half year ended September 30, 2026, consolidated revenue stood at ₹3,363.43 crore against ₹2,567.62 crore in the corresponding period last year. Half-year net profit came in at ₹352.19 crore compared to ₹335.78 crore previously. 

The company operates two business segments — Services and Technology Solutions. Services revenue for the quarter was ₹1,355.65 crore, while Technology Solutions contributed ₹343.15 crore. Basic earnings per share for the quarter stood at ₹4.22.

...

### Groww posts 54% jump in Q2 net profit, revenue surges 47% yoy 

Billionbrains Garage Ventures Limited, the parent company of investment platform Groww, on Wednesday reported a consolidated net profit of ₹724.70 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, a 54 per cent rise from ₹471.34 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations climbed 47 per cent year-on-year to ₹1,501.53 crore. 

For the first half of FY2026-27, consolidated net profit reached ₹1,459.74 crore against ₹849.69 crore in the year-ago period, while revenue from operations stood at ₹3,002.95 crore compared to ₹1,923.14 crore.

...

### Canara Bank posts 8.4% rise in net profit for Q2 FY27; asset quality improves sharply 

Canara Bank on Wednesday reported a net profit of ₹5,175 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 8.40 per cent year-on-year, driven by robust loan growth and a significant improvement in asset quality. 

The state-owned lender’s global business grew 15.88 per cent year-on-year to ₹30,72,365 crore. Global deposits rose 13.13 per cent to ₹16,97,305 crore, while global advances expanded 19.46 per cent to ₹13,75,060 crore. Operating profit stood at ₹8,758 crore, up 1.98 per cent over the same period last year. 

On the asset quality front, the bank’s gross NPA ratio fell sharply to 1.33 per cent from 2.35 per cent a year ago, while the net NPA ratio improved to 0.30 per cent from 0.54 per cent. The Provision Coverage Ratio strengthened to 95.34 per cent, up 175 basis points year-on-year. The slippage ratio stood at 0.58 per cent, improving by 18 basis points.

items.title: Earnings Central: Wipro, TechM, Polycab and Nestlé lead a busy Q2 results day - CNBC TV18
items.author: Sheersh Kapoor
items.text:
## Bonus issues, record dividends, surprise rallies and stocks sliding despite strong results. Thursday’s earnings rush had it all, from Wipro, TechM and Persistent Systems to Jio Financial Services, Polycab, Nestlé India and Tata Communications. Here’s your Q2 FY27 recap in Earnings Central.

Earnings Central

Q2 FY27 | October 15, 2026

Thursday was the kind of day that reminds you why earnings season is never short on drama. Bonus issues, record dividends, heavyweight IT names, FMCG giants, banks and NBFCs all had their moment. If Wednesday felt like a warm-up, Thursday was the main event. Here’s how the numbers stacked up, and where the surprises lay.

...

IT: Wipro stays steady, Tech Mahindra grabs attention, Persistent keeps powering ahead

Wipro’s Q2 was broadly in line with expectations. Dollar revenue dipped marginally to $2,611.5 million, while EBIT margin expanded by 50 basis points to 16.5%. Its Q3 revenue guidance of -1.5% to +0.5% sequentially also landed within the range the Street had anticipated. Steady, if not spectacular.

Tech Mahindra had a little more to offer. Net profit rose 8.2% quarter on quarter to ₹1,586 crore, dollar revenue grew 2%, and margins expanded for the 12th consecutive quarter. But it was the shareholder payouts that grabbed attention. The company announced a 1:1 bonus issue, its first since 2015, alongside an interim dividend of ₹15 per share.

Persistent Systems, meanwhile, continued to build on its growth streak, notching up its 26th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. Rupee revenue rose 30.3% year on year to ₹4,663.9 crore. Reported profit after tax took a hit from an exceptional expense of ₹185.34 crore related to the proposed Nagarro acquisition.

...

Financial services: Strong numbers, but not every stock got the same response

It was a busy day for financial services, with growth showing up across lending, insurance, banking and broking. The details, however, mattered.

Jio Financial Services kept up its rapid expansion. Total income, excluding dividend income, more than doubled year on year to ₹1,699 crore. Its lending arm, Jio Credit, reported a 140% jump in profit after tax, while assets under management surged 154% to ₹37,320 crore. The scale-up is becoming increasingly visible in the numbers.

IIFL Finance also delivered a strong quarter. Net profit more than doubled year on year to ₹766.4 crore, net interest income rose 50%, and assets under management grew 38% to ₹1.24 lakh crore. Gross non-performing assets stood at 1.5%, keeping asset quality in focus alongside the growth.

HDFC Life turned in a steady performance, with net profit rising 13.6% to ₹508 crore. V alue of new business grew 12.1% in the first half of FY27, while new business margins edged higher. It was a quarter of consistent progress rather than a headline-grabbing surprise.

IRFC reported a 10.2% increase in net profit to ₹1,958.5 crore and maintained its zero-NPA record. It also declared its highest-ever single-tranche interim dividend of ₹1.50 per share, putting shareholder returns firmly in the spotlight.

Among the banks, Karur Vysya Bank stood out. Profit rose 37.2% year on year to ₹788 crore, net interest income increased 19%, and gross NPAs came in at a low 0.69%.

Angel One staged a strong sequential recovery, with net profit jumping 44.7% quarter on quarter and EBITDA margin widening to 44.6%.

Indian Bank offered a reminder that headline numbers do not always tell the whole story. Profit rose 14.7% and net interest income grew 17.8%, yet the stock fell more than 3%. A one-time gain linked to the NSE share listing contributed to other income, and investors appeared to look beyond the reported growth. UCO Bank and the broader PSU banking pack, meanwhile, delivered numbers that were largely in line with expectations.

...

Beyond the banks: Polycab shines, Nestlé slips, Tata Communications bounces back

Polycab was one of the day’s standout performer s. Net profit jumped 42.6% year on year to ₹977 crore, comfortably ahead of poll estimates, while revenue surged 53% to ₹9,899 crore. Strong execution across its wires and cables business, along with growth in FMCG, helped drive the performance.

Nestlé India’s quarter was more puzzling from a market perspective. Net profit rose 36.4% to ₹1,027 crore and revenue grew 20.3%, with both broadly in line with estimates. Yet the stock fell more than 7%. Meeting expectations can still disappoint when investors are looking for something more.

Tata Communications, on the other hand, staged a strong recovery during the session. Net profit surged 86.3% year on year to ₹341 crore, while digital losses halved. The stock bounced sharply from its intraday lows, giving the results a more positive market reception.

Heritage Foods faced a tougher quarter. Profit fell 38.6% even as revenue rose 18.6%, with higher milk procurement costs putting pressure on margins. Its value-added products business continues to grow, but rising input costs remain a challenge.

---

items.title: Nestle India stock falls further after 8% crash on Q2 results
items.author: Shaleen Agrawal
items.text:
Q2 results; HSBC sees 16% upside but flags growth slowdown

Nestle India shares fell further after an 8 percent plunge following Q2 results. HSBC maintained its Hold rating with a Rs 1,480 target price, implying 16 percent upside, but warned of moderating growth in H2 FY27.

...

Shaleen Agrawal October 16, 2026 / 09:26 IST 

 

Nestle India Ltd

- Nestle India shares dropped further following Q2 earnings.
- Consolidated net profit surged 35.9 percent to Rs 1,009.6 cr.
- Management highlighted rising food inflation and cost pressures.

...

Nestle India shares extended their losses on Friday after plunging nearly 8 percent in the previous session following the company's fiscal second quarter earnings. Brokerage HSBC maintained its 'Hold' rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 1,480, implying an upside of around 16 percent from Thursday's closing price. It cautioned that revenue growth could moderate in the second half of FY27.

Nestle India shares declined 1.05 percent to Rs 1,262.40 in early trade on Friday, extending Thursday's 7.8 percent slump. Despite the sharp two-day decline, the stock remained down just 1.5 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen around 12 percent during the same period. The company's market capitalisation stood at Rs 2.46 lakh crore.

...

HSBC said that Nestle India's revenue grew around 20 percent year-on-year in the July-September quarter, broadly in line with estimates, while its two-year revenue compound annual growth rate (CAGR) stood at 15 percent. EBITDA exceeded consensus expectations by approximately 3 percent.

The brokerage highlighted sequential improvement in Nestle India's nutrition business, while chocolates and coffee continued to deliver strong performance. However, HSBC cautioned that the company's growth momentum could moderate in the second half of the financial year.

...

Nestle India reported a 35.9 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 1,009.6 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, while revenue from operations rose 20.3 percent to Rs 6,788.3 crore. On a standalone basis, net profit rose 36.2 percent to Rs 1,026.8 crore, exceeding CNBC-TV18's poll estimate of Rs 1,018 crore. Standalone revenue increased 20.3 percent to Rs 6,788.3 crore, broadly matching the poll estimate of Rs 6,789 crore.

Despite the strong quarterly performance, Nestle India shares came under heavy selling pressure on Thursday as the company's management highlighted rising inflation and continued commodity cost challenges. "Rising inflation, particularly food inflation, is a reality," Chairman and Managing Director Manish Tiwary said, adding that the company would focus on productivity improvements and operational efficiencies to mitigate commodity cost pressures.

Nestle India said coffee and wheat prices were expected to remain range-bound, while sugar and edible oil prices had stabilised at elevated levels. Cocoa prices remained volatile due to weather-related concerns, while milk prices had strengthened seasonally but were expected to ease with the arrival of flush supplies. The company reported broad-based growth across product groups, supported by double-digit volume growth, with domestic sales rising 20.4 percent during the quarter.

---

Q2 Results Highlights Updates: Thursday was the kind of day that reminds you why earnings season is never short on drama. Bonus issues, record dividends, heavyweight IT names, FMCG giants, banks and NBFCs all had their moment. If Wednesday felt like a warm-up, Thursday was the main event. Wipro’s Q2 was broadly in line with expectations. Dollar revenue dipped marginally to $2,611.5 million, while EBIT margin expanded by 50 basis points to 16.5%. Tech Mahindra had a little more to offer. Net profit rose 8.2% quarter on quarter to ₹1,586 crore, dollar revenue grew 2%, and margins expanded for the 12th consecutive quarter. But it was the shareholder payouts that grabbed attention. Persistent Systems, meanwhile, continued to build on its growth streak, notching up its 26th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. HDFC Life turned in a steady performance, with net profit rising 13.6% to ₹508 crore. Value of new business grew 12.1% in the first half of FY27, while new business margins edged higher. It was a quarter of consistent progress rather than a headline-grabbing surprise.
